title: Ice-age crustal rebound as the cause of pole shift
place_text: North America, Hudson Bay, northwestern Europe

tellings.quote: I think that what happens is is that with the process of glaciation, rapid glaciation or rapid deglaciation, it induces a tremendous amount of instability in the Earth's crust that could manifest as an accelerated episode of continental of of lithospheric movement.

plain: When ice ages come and go quickly, the weight of ice building up or melting over places like Hudson Bay and northwestern Europe could shake the Earth's outer shell loose enough to slide, moving whole continents relative to the poles. The researcher Randall Carlson offers this as his own view, building on the writer Charles Hapgood and a talk he gave on Atlantis, saying rapid glaciation or deglaciation "induces a tremendous amount of instability in the Earth's crust." If true, it would mean the poles can shift fast enough to remake the world within human memory.
